findings.title: Invalidate native authentication when its provider unmounts
findings.scenario: Provider A starts login and waits. Unmount A. Mount provider B and finish replacement login for user 8, storing replacement-access/replacement-refresh. Resolve A login with late-old-access/late-old-refresh.
findings.expected: The old provider cannot overwrite replacement durable credentials or workspace, and late minted credentials are revoked against their captured original origin.
findings.observed: Independent focused component reproduction fails: writeStoredTokens final call is late-old-access/late-old-refresh, after replacement tokens were written. Provider B UI still represents user 8. This is synthetic component execution against unchanged reviewed source, not physical-device execution.
findings.cause: Native cleanup only sets the hydrate-local isMounted=false. It does not invalidate sessionEpochRef/targetReady/accountScopeRef for login/refresh closures. The late login still passes its old provider epoch check and persistAuthPayload writes through shared storage.
findings.consequence: After remount and account replacement, persisted identity can revert to the old account and disagree with the active UI. It violates the PR’s account/session isolation claim. No claim of production exploitation or baseline-introduced regression is made.
findings.correction: Owner must invalidate the native provider lifetime synchronously on cleanup; guard outstanding login/register/refresh and persistence awaits against that lifetime and replacement session. Preserve replacement tokens/cache, prevent old callbacks accessing or clearing replacement credentials, and queue/revoke late minted credentials using their captured origin. Add maintained native remount regressions covering late login and refresh, then rerun affected tests. Do not merely adjust the mock or timeout.

findings.title: Reconcile the final behavior claim after the isolation fix
findings.observed: The final body claims old callbacks cannot affect replacement sessions and says independent QA remains pending. The remount case now disproves the unconditional behavior claim.
findings.correction: After R1 correction, update the existing final Test plan to reflect the observed remount regression and current QA state, retaining pending device limitations. Submit the exact final body for reread; do not rewrite historical evidence.
